config.title: Berlin School Registration - FAQ
config.subtitle: The October window, how to find the Grundschule your address is assigned to, what to bring, how a request for a different school is actually decided, deferral and early entry, and the compulsory language test.

items.q: When is school registration in Berlin?
items.a: The registration window for the 2027/28 school year runs from 5 to 16 October 2026, ten working days. You register in person at the primary school your address is assigned to, and the Senate recommends bringing the child. It applies to every child born between 1 October 2020 and 30 September 2021, who becomes subject to compulsory schooling on 1 August 2027. There is no online alternative to the main appointment, although the application for a different school can be pre-filled online and brought printed and signed.

items.q: How do I find out which Grundschule my address is assigned to?
items.a: Berlin is divided into Einschulungsbereiche, catchment areas drawn by each Bezirk, and the one your flat sits in names the school. Your Bezirksschulamt writes to you with the name, and it is normally the nearest public Grundschule. The Senate publishes the boundaries as open geodata: measured from that data on 17 September 2026 there are 394 catchment areas containing 413 public primary schools, so 356 areas hold exactly one school, 28 hold two or three, and 10 hold none inside the boundary at all. The catchment map on this page draws all of them.

items.q: What do I need to bring to the registration appointment?
items.a: Your own identity papers, the child’s birth certificate, any other identity papers for the child, the application for ergänzende Förderung und Betreuung (the after-school Hort place) if you want one, and anything that helps the school understand your child’s needs. The registration form itself is produced by the school at the desk and you sign it there, so there is nothing to print in advance except the wish-school application if you are making one.

items.q: Can I choose a different primary school in Berlin?
items.a: You can ask for one, but the sequence is fixed. First register at the assigned school, then submit a written application with reasons for the school you want. The Bezirksschulamt decides under § 55a Abs. 2 of the Berlin Schulgesetz, which ranks the grounds: damage to long standing personal ties to other children and siblings above all, then a specific school programme, foreign language or all-day model, then care of the child being significantly easier because of your working hours. Distance is not one of the listed grounds, and any request is only granted if that school still has places after its own catchment children are placed.

items.q: What if my assigned school is a gebundene Ganztagsschule and I do not want that?
items.a: You do not have to argue your way out through the wish-school process. If the assigned school runs the bound all-day model and you do not want that pedagogical offer for your child, the district places the child in one of its open all-day schools instead. Say so at registration. For scale: of the 392 public Grundschulen offering care from 6:00 to 18:00, 330 (84.2%) use the open model, 41 (10.5%) are gebundene Ganztagsschulen, and 21 run both class by class.

items.q: Can my child start school a year later in Berlin?
items.a: Yes. A Zurückstellung is decided by the Schulaufsicht and granted when a further year of targeted support in a Kita is genuinely the better path. You need a statement from the Kita, a school medical examination by the end of February 2027, and the application itself by 26 February 2027. It can be used only once and is impossible after school has started. It is more common than most parents expect: of the 35,571 children Berlin enrolled in 2025/26, 4,547 (12.8%) arrived after a deferral.

items.q: Can my child start school a year early in Berlin?
items.a: Only for a narrow birth window and only on one condition. A child born between 1 October 2021 and 31 March 2022 can be put forward on application, provided the child needs no language support, which is proven with a QuaSta form or the BeoKiz language assessment. A child born after 31 March 2022 cannot start before summer 2028. It is rare: in 2025/26 just 720 children, 2.0% of the intake, came in this way.

items.q: Is the Berlin language test before school compulsory?
items.a: Yes, for children who do not attend a Kita. Participation is required under § 55 of the Berlin Schulgesetz. If the assessment shows a need, the child must attend pre-school language support of 35 hours a week, seven hours a day across five days, running until 31 July before enrolment. Missing it is an Ordnungswidrigkeit and can be fined up to 2,500 euros under § 126 of the same law. Children already in a Kita are assessed inside the Kita, and their parents have nothing separate to arrange.

items.q: How long does primary school last in Berlin?
items.a: Six years, not the four that most other German states use. Years one and two are taught together as a flexible Schulanfangsphase, which a child can cross in two years or in three. That is why the October appointment carries more weight here than the same appointment elsewhere: the school you register at is usually the next six years of school runs and parents’ evenings.

items.q: What happens after the registration appointment?
items.a: The Kinder- und Jugendgesundheitsdienst examines your child, and you get the booking information at registration. The Schulamt of your district, not the school at the door, allocates the place, and in individual cases it can place a child at a different Grundschule for organisational reasons and writes to tell you. If you applied for a Hort place, the Jugendamt sends a Bedarfsbescheid and you then sign a contract with the Jugendamt or the provider. The Einschulungsfeier is normally Saturday 21 August 2027, regular lessons begin Monday 23 August 2027, and Hort care can start from 1 August 2027.
